projectDesc.p: The Welte-Mignon Advertisements Collection brings together print advertisements for the Welte-Mignon reproducing piano that appeared between 1905 and 1930. It was created as part of the PhD project "Grünfelds Geist" at the University of Tübingen, which considers piano rolls as objects of a digital edition. The collection is published at https://anz.welte225.org.

samplingDecl.p: The collection gathers print advertisements for the Welte-Mignon reproducing piano that appeared between 1905 and 1930 and were published by M. Welte & Söhne, by one of its licensees, or by a dealer or agent selling the instrument. Each advertisement is encoded once; its further printings, in the same or in other periodicals, are listed as further sources.

The advertisements were found in digitised newspapers and magazines: Chronicling America (Library of Congress), the British Newspaper Archive, HathiTrust (copies of the Universities of California, Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota and Virginia), the Internet Archive, the Digitale Sammlungen of the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, ANNO (Austrian National Library), the International Arcade Museum Library, Georgia Historic Newspapers, Delpher (KB, National Library of the Netherlands), eluxemburgensia (National Library of Luxembourg), RetroNews (Bibliothèque nationale de France), the archives of Le Temps, the Nasjonalbiblioteket of Norway, Mediestream (Royal Danish Library), the National Library of Latvia (through Europeana), Canadiana, the Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México, the St Petersburg State Theatre Library, Trove (National Library of Australia), the newspapers of the Kungliga biblioteket of Sweden, e-newspaperarchives.ch, BAnQ numérique (Bibliothèque et Archives nationales du Québec), the Biblioteca Virtual de Prensa Histórica, the archive of ABC and ARCA (Biblioteca de Catalunya).

editorialDecl.p: Each file transcribes one printing of an advertisement, the one whose scan its facsimile zones refer to; decls on text points to its sourceDesc. The further printings were identified as the same advertisement but not collated word for word; differences that were noticed are recorded with app or in a note.

The regions and lines of the scans were mostly marked in eScriptorium and converted from PAGE XML to TEI. The text was in part recognised automatically (HTR) and corrected against the scan, in part transcribed by hand. The advertisements published outside Germany, the United Kingdom and the United States were transcribed from the scans, encoded, given their regions and annotated with topics by Claude, an AI model; their revision history says so.

correction.p: Errors of the original are not corrected but marked with sic.

normalization.p: Spelling and punctuation follow the original and are not normalised. Text set in capitals is often transcribed in mixed case and marked with the rendition #uc.

hyphenation.p: Hyphens at the end of a line are kept as printed.

segmentation.p: Every region of the original page is a div that points to its zone in the facsimile with facs. The lines of the original are marked with lb; the typography is recorded with rendition. The zones refer to the first graphic of a surface, the scan they were drawn on. Where the holding library serves the page through IIIF, a second graphic of the type IIIF gives that image and its size.

interpretation.p: Parts of an advertisement that concern other products than the Welte-Mignon are not transcribed but marked with gap, which describes them in a desc. Illustrations are described in figure. Persons are linked to the GND with corresp. Recurring motifs are marked as topics with ana on seg and figure, pointing to the taxonomy of topics; these are an interpretation, by whom resp says.

stdVals.p: Dates of publication are given in ISO 8601 in when, as precisely as they are known.

taxonomy.desc: Topics: recurring motifs of the advertisements, in their texts and in their pictures

category.desc: In virtually all promotional materials between 1905 and 1926, the claim of exact and faithful reproduction, of absolute accurateness is consistently emphasized.
This topic emphasizes the perdurance of the reproductions and how thus the recording artists become immortal.
The Welte-Mignon is permanently available and "objectified" for the entertainment of the owner – on the touch of a button.

revisionDesc.change: Transcribed from the scan, encoded, zones drawn and topics annotated by Claude; not yet checked by the editor.

head.hi: After many inventions and many failures—A PERFECT INSTRUMENT.

div.p:
AN INSTRUMENT OF REPRODUCTION. Exact and individual renderings of Classical Music played by the
World's greatest Pianists.

“WELTE” PLAYER can be attached to any ordinary Upright or Horizontal Piano, and is actuated by electricity
instead of foot power. This attachment represents the highest possible development of the pneumatic piano-player, inasmuch
as it furnishes a reproduction of the actual interpretation placed upon the written score of a great composer by the great modern
executant. In the words of a well-known musician, “It is a photograph.”

OPERATION.—After the insertion of the perforated roll, a button is pressed which starts the motor; the tempo lever
is set to the mark which represents the exact time at which the artist played.
Every piece rendered with distinction, for over 100 artists of renown have played for this instrument.

It immortalises a single performance so that the touch of a pianist who has even now passed away, may be handed
down to remote posterity.
The regret of musicians must ever be that this great invention was not brought out in 1809 instead of 1909.

head.hi: OPINIONS OF THE WORLD'S FAMOUS MUSICIANS:

p.quote:
“My ADMIRATION of the greatest invention which bears the name of
‘WELTE’ is unlimited. In my opinion it is the most amazing of all inven-
tions which have hitherto been made in the field of musical instruments, and its
name will become known and create the greatest sensation throughout the
world.”

“I had heard a great deal about the ‘WELTE,’ and am more than de-
lighted after having heard it played. What I found most astonishing was the
perfect reproduction of touch, even to the finest shadings. In short, the
‘WELTE’ is not only human, but superhuman.”

p.hi: Testimonies by other famous musicians may be seen on application.

div.p: This INSTRUMENT is for you to SEE and HEAR. Public are cordially invited to DAILY RECITALS.
